Grade appeals require supporting documentation. Possible grounds include a computational error, factual information unavailable when the grade was posted (such as submitted work that was not graded), or an alleged College Policy violation. Appeals based only on wanting a higher grade or challenging an Academic Integrity penalty are not considered. A degree’s record is closed after the degree is conferred. [1]

**Undergraduate:** No later than 20 calendar days after grades are posted, email or send a certified letter to the course instructor, with supporting documentation. You and the instructor have up to 15 calendar days to reach a determination. If you cannot agree, submit a written appeal by email or certified letter to the Dean of the academic unit that sponsored the course within 20 calendar days of the final determination conference; include pertinent course materials or coursework. The Dean has 15 calendar days to decide. If the Dean does not support the appeal, you may petition the Office of the Provost within 20 calendar days of the Dean’s final written determination. Submit a written statement by email or certified letter explaining your position and including evidence contradicting the Dean’s decision or information previously unavailable. The Provost may reject petitions without clear evidence of a factual mistake, policy violation, or action outside the Dean’s purview; appeals must first have been fully considered by the instructor and Dean. [2]

**Graduate:** The initial deadline is also 20 calendar days after grades are posted; write to the faculty member by email or certified letter and provide supporting documentation. You have up to 15 calendar days to reach a determination. If you cannot agree, submit a written appeal with pertinent course materials or coursework to the sponsoring graduate program’s Director within 20 calendar days of the final determination conference. The Director’s decision is a recommendation to the Dean for final approval. If the Director does not support the appeal, you may petition the Dean who supervises the program. The page excerpt does not give a deadline for that petition. [3]

For the applicable procedure, contact the Office of the Provost.

Start with the Office of Specialized Services (OSS): students requesting a medically related housing accommodation must register/affiliate with OSS and initiate contact. See “How To Request OSS Services” for information: [https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/how-to-request-oss-services/](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/how-to-request-oss-services/) [3]

Submit comprehensive disability documentation from a licensed physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, social worker, or certified learning disabilities specialist. Documentation may be a report following OSS guidelines or the form for the disability; for a medical impairment, OSS lists a writable Medical Impairments Documentation Form: [https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/wp-content/uploads/sites/137/2020/06/Medical-Impairments-Documentation-Form-fillable-2-6-2020.pdf](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/wp-content/uploads/sites/137/2020/06/Medical-Impairments-Documentation-Form-fillable-2-6-2020.pdf) [3][8][9]

Complete an Affiliation Packet. Request it using the OSS Quick Response Form [https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/oss-quick-response-form/](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/oss-quick-response-form/) or contact OSS by email; send the completed packet and supporting documentation electronically to OSS. [9]

Then submit the housing accommodation request forms through the OSS Housing Accommodations page: [https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/). The page notes that students requesting only a strobe alarm, roll-in shower, wheelchair/mobility accessible residence hall, or first floor do not need the Housing Accommodation Student or Provider Request Forms, but do need a request for disability support form. OSS reviews the request, usually with the Housing Accommodation Request Committee. A decision can be expected within 21 business days after OSS receives all requested documentation; OSS may ask for more information. [4][6] Once affiliated, OSS informs Residence Life of approved accommodation needs. Submit by Residence Life’s published deadlines: accommodations depend on availability and are not guaranteed; a late request may prevent Residence Life from meeting an approved accommodation for the requested semester. The Office of the Provost says grade appeals require supporting documentation. Possible grounds include a computational error, factual information not considered when the grade was posted, or an alleged College Policy violation. Appeals based only on wanting a higher grade, or on a grade penalty for an Academic Integrity violation, will not be considered. A degree’s academic record is closed after the degree is conferred. [1]

If you are an undergraduate: within twenty calendar days after grades are posted, bring the appeal to your course instructor in writing by email or certified letter, with supporting documentation. You and the instructor have up to 15 calendar days to reach a determination. If you agree on an adjustment, the instructor sends an Instructor Grade Adjustment Request and supporting documentation to the course’s Dean for approval, then to the Registrar. If you do not agree, submit a written appeal by email or certified letter, with pertinent course materials or coursework, to the Dean within twenty calendar days of the final determination conference. The Dean has 15 calendar days to decide. If the Dean does not support your appeal, you may petition the Office of the Provost within twenty calendar days of the Dean’s final written determination, by written statement via email or certified letter, explaining your position and including contradictory evidence or previously unavailable information. The Provost may reject petitions without clear evidence of a factual mistake, policy violation, or action outside the Dean’s purview. [2]

If you are a graduate student: within twenty calendar days after grades are posted, appeal in writing by email or certified letter to the faculty member, with supporting documentation. You and the faculty member have up to 15 calendar days to reach a determination. If unresolved, submit a written appeal by email or certified letter, with pertinent course materials or coursework, to the graduate program Director within twenty calendar days of the final determination conference. The Director’s decision is a recommendation to the Dean for final approval. [3]

Start with the Office of Specialized Services (OSS): register for affiliation and initiate contact. See “How To Request OSS Services” ([https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/how-to-request-oss-services/](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/how-to-request-oss-services/)). Submit comprehensive disability documentation from a licensed physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, social worker, or certified learning disabilities specialist to establish eligibility and determine appropriate accommodations. See OSS’s housing-accommodations page for the appropriate forms and the Housing Accommodation Request Policy: [https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/) and [https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/wp-content/uploads/sites/137/2024/03/1-Housing-Accommodation-Request-Policy-updated-3-7-24.pdf](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/wp-content/uploads/sites/137/2024/03/1-Housing-Accommodation-Request-Policy-updated-3-7-24.pdf). [3][5][7]
If requesting only a strobe alarm, roll-in shower, wheelchair/mobility accessible residence hall, or 1st floor, you do not need the Housing Accommodation Student or Provider Request Forms; complete only a request for disability support form. [3]
OSS reviews your request and, in most cases, the Housing Accommodation Request Committee reviews it. Decisions are typically within twenty one (21) business days after OSS receives all requested documentation. OSS may request more information or contact the professional who provided it. [4][6]
Once affiliated, OSS informs the Office of Residence Life of approved housing needs based on your medical documentation; Residence Life works with OSS on placement. Housing is subject to availability, and accessible housing is limited, first-come-first-served, and not guaranteed. Submit by Residence Life’s published deadlines; a late request may prevent an approved accommodation from being met for the requested semester. [1][2][6][7]

Yes, but only with an approved disability accommodation; the College may limit the animal to defined campus areas, and it generally will not be permitted in academic or recreational facilities. [2][3]

The Office of Specialized Services (OSS) handles the process:
1. Call 201-684-7514 to discuss your interest; OSS will schedule a meeting with its Director. [1]
2. Register with OSS and submit comprehensive disability documentation from a licensed physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, social worker, or certified learning disabilities specialist. Documentation must demonstrate the benefits provided by the animal. [2][5]
3. Submit the Animal Documentation Form: [https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/wp-content/uploads/sites/137/2022/07/Animal-Documentation-Form-fillable-updated-7-5-22.pdf](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/wp-content/uploads/sites/137/2022/07/Animal-Documentation-Form-fillable-updated-7-5-22.pdf) [7]
4. OSS staff, and in most cases the Housing Accommodation Request Committee, review the request. Allow time for the process; once approved, OSS works with Residence Life on placement. Submit housing requests by the published deadlines. [6][12]

OSS and/or the committee may deny a request if it is unreasonable or insufficiently documented. Reasons can include inadequate evidence, a condition that does not meet the definition of disability, undue burden, fundamental alteration of housing policy, or a direct threat/substantial property damage. For an ESA, the College may also inquire about the animal’s age and size/breed, if applicable. [4]

See the Emotional Support Animal Policy: [https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/campus-accessibility-and-services-information/service-support-animal-policy/](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/campus-accessibility-and-services-information/service-support-animal-policy/) [1][2]

The Office of the Provost’s catalog says grade appeals require supporting documentation. Possible grounds include a computational error, factual information not considered when the grade was posted, or an alleged College Policy violation. Appeals based only on wanting a higher grade, or on a grade penalty for an Academic Integrity violation, will not be considered. [1]

For an undergraduate: Within 20 calendar days after grades are posted, write to the course instructor by email or certified letter and provide supporting documentation. You and the instructor have up to 15 calendar days to reach a determination. If you cannot agree, submit a written appeal, with pertinent course materials or coursework, to the Dean of the academic unit that sponsored the course within 20 calendar days of the final determination conference. The Dean has 15 calendar days to decide. If the Dean’s written determination does not support your appeal, you may petition the Office of the Provost by written statement, email or certified letter, within 20 calendar days of that determination. The petition must include evidence contradicting the Dean’s decision or previously unavailable information; it must clearly show a factual mistake, policy violation, or action outside the Dean’s purview. [2]

For a graduate student: The initial instructor appeal and 20-calendar-day deadline, documentation, and up-to-15-day discussion period are the same. If you cannot agree, submit a written appeal with pertinent course materials or coursework to the graduate program Director within 20 calendar days of the final determination conference. If the Director’s opinion does not support your appeal, you may petition the Dean who supervises the program with a written statement and evidence contradicting the Director’s decision or previously unavailable information. The page gives no deadline for that petition. [3]

Yes, an emotional support animal may be permitted as a disability accommodation, but approval is required and it may be limited to defined campus areas; it generally is not allowed in academic or recreational facilities. [2][3]

The Office of Specialized Services (OSS) handles the request:
1. First register with OSS. You must initiate contact and submit comprehensive disability documentation from a licensed physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, social worker, or certified learning disabilities specialist. See “How To Request OSS Services.” [5]
2. Call 201-684-7514 to discuss your interest. OSS will schedule a meeting with its Director. See the Emotional Support Animal Policy for more information. [1]
3. Provide documentation demonstrating the benefits of the animal. The request is reviewed by OSS and, in most cases, the Housing Accommodation Request Committee; if approved, OSS works with Residence Life on placement. [2][6]
4. The Animal Documentation Form is available here: [https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/wp-content/uploads/sites/137/2022/07/Animal-Documentation-Form-fillable-updated-7-5-22.pdf](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/wp-content/uploads/sites/137/2022/07/Animal-Documentation-Form-fillable-updated-7-5-22.pdf) [7]

OSS and/or the committee may deny a request if it is unreasonable or insufficiently documented. Factors include whether documentation supports the request, undue burden, changes to housing policy, or health, safety, or property risks; the College may inquire about the animal’s age, size, or breed. [4] Submit housing requests by Residence Life’s published deadlines. [12]

The Office of the Provost says grade appeals require supporting documentation. Possible grounds include a computational error, factual information not considered when the grade was posted, or an alleged College Policy violation. Appeals based only on wanting a higher grade, or on grades penalized for an Academic Integrity violation, will not be considered. After a degree is conferred, its academic record cannot be adjusted. [1]

For an undergraduate course, email or send a certified letter to the instructor with your appeal and supporting documentation no later than twenty calendar days after grades are posted. You and the instructor have up to 15 calendar days to reach a determination. If you cannot agree, submit a written appeal with pertinent course materials or coursework to the Dean of the academic unit that sponsored the course within twenty calendar days of the final determination conference. If the Dean does not support your appeal, you may petition the Office of the Provost in writing by email or certified letter within twenty calendar days of the Dean’s final written determination, including your position and evidence contradicting the decision or previously unavailable information. The Provost may reject a petition unless it clearly shows the Dean made a factual mistake, violated College policy, or acted outside the Dean’s purview. [2]

For a graduate course, email or send a certified letter to the faculty member with your appeal and supporting documentation no later than twenty calendar days after grades are posted. You and the faculty member have up to 15 calendar days to reach a determination. If you cannot agree, submit a written appeal with pertinent course materials or coursework to the sponsoring graduate program’s Director within twenty calendar days of the final determination conference. The Office of the Provost says grade appeals require documentation. Possible grounds include a computational error, factual information not considered when the grade was posted, or an alleged College Policy violation. Appeals based only on wanting a higher grade, or grades penalized for an Academic Integrity Policy violation, are not considered. [1]

The procedures differ for undergraduate and graduate students:
- Undergraduate: Within 20 calendar days after grades are posted, email or send a certified letter with supporting documentation to the course instructor. Both parties should make good-faith efforts to discuss the issue; they have up to 15 calendar days to reach a determination. If unresolved, submit a written appeal by email or certified letter, with pertinent course materials or coursework, to the Dean of the academic unit that sponsored the course, within 20 calendar days of the final determination conference. The Dean has 15 calendar days to decide. If the Dean’s opinion does not support your appeal, you may petition the Office of the Provost in writing by email or certified letter within 20 calendar days of the Dean’s final written determination. The petition must explain your position and include evidence contradicting the Dean’s decision or previously unavailable information. The Provost may reject it if it does not clearly show factual error, a policy violation, or action outside the Dean’s purview; the appeal must first have had full deliberative discussion at instructor and Dean level. [2]
- Graduate: Within 20 calendar days after grades are posted, email or send a certified letter with supporting documentation to the faculty member. They have up to 15 calendar days to reach a determination. If unresolved, send a written appeal by email or certified letter, with pertinent course materials or coursework, to the Director of the graduate program that sponsored the course, within 20 calendar days of the final determination conference. [3]

A separate procedure page says to begin preferably as soon as you believe you have grounds, and no later than 20 calendar days after the last day of the semester. It says you may meet with the instructor or, with a compelling case, the Dean; if unresolved, appeal to the Dean within 20 calendar days after the instructor conference. The Dean has 15 calendar days to decide. [14]

The Office of Specialized Services (OSS) handles disability-related housing accommodations. An emotional support animal is permitted on campus only as an approved disability accommodation; it may be limited to defined campus areas and generally is not permitted in academic or recreational facilities. [2][3]

1. Call OSS at (201) 684-7514 to discuss your interest. Interested students will be scheduled to meet with the OSS Director. [1]
2. First register with OSS. Initiate contact and submit comprehensive disability documentation from a licensed physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, social worker, or certified learning disabilities specialist. See “How To Request OSS Services”: [https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/how-to-request-oss-services/](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/how-to-request-oss-services/) [5]
3. Submit the Animal Documentation Form: [https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/wp-content/uploads/sites/137/2022/07/Animal-Documentation-Form-fillable-updated-7-5-22.pdf](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/wp-content/uploads/sites/137/2022/07/Animal-Documentation-Form-fillable-updated-7-5-22.pdf) [6] Submit the appropriate housing forms through the Housing Accommodations page: [https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/) [7]
4. OSS and/or the Housing Accommodation Request Committee determine whether the request is reasonable. It may be denied if the condition is not a disability, evidence is inadequate, it creates an undue financial or administrative burden, fundamentally alters housing policy, or poses a direct threat or substantial property-damage risk. For an ESA, the College may also inquire about the animal’s age, size/breed. [4]
5. If affiliated, OSS informs Residence Life of approved housing needs. Submit requests by Residence Life’s published deadlines; accommodations are first-come-first-served, not guaranteed, and depend on availability. A late request may prevent Residence Life from meeting an approved accommodation for the requested semester. [7][11][12]
